title: Task & reference-metric framework for evaluating FP8/INT8 quant profiles
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description: We need a general, extensible framework to compute and report quality metrics across FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles that will be used as the primary gate for model release and automated rollbacks. The framework must support: token-weighted perplexity, stratified MMLU-style task suites, reference-based metrics (ROUGE/BLEU) with normalized scoring, and task-specific scorers (e.g., F1 for NER, accuracy for classification, execution checks for code). It should run in CI, integrate with the Console reports, and produce human-readable artifacts for SRE/QA to assess regressions and tuning decisions. Key goals: repeatability across hardware, signal separation between quantization noise and model drift, and per-customer impact tagging for rollout decisions.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible job definition (YAML) that runs the full metric suite for a given model + quant profile and emits a single compressed artifact (JSON + CSV + HTML)
Per-task metrics computed: token-weighted perplexity, MMLU-style aggregated accuracy, ROUGE-L and BLEU-4 with length-normalization, and task-specific scorers where applicable
Statistical significance tests (bootstrap) across baseline FP32 and candidate quant profile with clear p-values and effect sizes
CI gate integration: jobs return success/failure with a machine-readable verdict and human-friendly HTML summary linked in the CI build
Baseline caching: ability to reuse cached FP32 baselines to avoid re-running expensive evaluations when the baseline model has not changed
Console integration: metric breakdown endpoints and sample failure cases available to Console QA dashboards and rollout tooling
updates: 2025-02-15: Ticket created. Initial scoping meeting with PM and Design to align on required metrics and SLAs. Decided to prioritize reproducibility and CI gating before fancy visualization.

2025-02-18: Prototype runner sketched using Airflow + containerized tasks. Trade-off: Airflow gives scheduling reliability but heavier infra; we will ship a thin runner for CI first and prototype Airflow for nightly aggregates.

2025-02-22: Chose metric implementations: token-weighted perplexity (perplexity computed on token-level log-probs, weighted by real token counts), exact-match + accuracy for MMLU-style suites, ROUGE-L & BLEU-4 using SacreBLEU config with length penalty normalization. Documented in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Quant+Quality+Metrics

2025-02-25: Decision: run bootstrap (N=1000) for significance instead of paired t-test to handle non-normal error distributions. Implementation note: use stratified bootstraps by task and difficulty band to preserve inter-task variance.

2025-02-28: Implemented local runner and smoke tests; added sample job definition and created PR #5234: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5234. Requesting design review for HTML report layout (DES-431).

2025-03-03: Integration spike shows INT8 profiles cause ~0.6% absolute MMLU accuracy drop on average for code-heavy prompts; added per-task tolerances and customer_impact tagging to help rollout decisions. Planning to add conversational turn-level checks next sprint.
notes: Design trade-offs: we will not attempt human-in-the-loop adjudication in phase 1; use automatic scorers and surface ambiguous examples for manual review in Console.
Performance: expensive evaluations (long-context perplexity suites) will be scheduled as nightly jobs; CI will run a lighter 'smoke' metric set to keep feedback fast.
Observability: store per-example delta logs (FP32 vs quant) for top-100 regressions to enable targeted kernel / quant tuning investigations
Rollout policy: automated rollback if task-weighted aggregate regression > threshold AND p-value < 0.01, otherwise mark yellow and require manual approval
